{{Short description|Spiral}}
{{one source |date=May 2024}}
[[image:lituus.svg|thumb|300px|Branch for positive {{mvar|r}}]]
The '''lituus''' spiral ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|l|ɪ|tj|u|.|ə|s}}) is a spiral in which the [[Polar coordinate system|polar angle]] {{mvar|θ}} is inversely proportional to the square of the radius {{mvar|r}}.

This spiral, which has two branches depending on the sign of {{mvar|r}}, is [[Asymptote|asymptotic]] to the {{mvar|x}} axis. Its [[points of inflexion]] are at

: <math>(\theta, r) = \left(\tfrac12, \pm\sqrt{2k}\right).</math>

The curve was named for the ancient Roman [[lituus]] by [[Roger Cotes]] in a collection of papers entitled ''Harmonia Mensurarum'' (1722), which was published six years after his death.

== Coordinate representations ==

=== Polar coordinates ===
The representations of the lituus spiral in [[Polar coordinate system|polar coordinates]] {{math|(''r'', ''θ'')}} is given by the equation

: <math>r = \frac{a}{\sqrt{\theta}},</math>

where {{math|''θ'' ≥ 0}} and {{math|''a'' ≠ 0}}.

=== Cartesian coordinates ===
The lituus spiral with the [[Polar coordinate system|polar coordinates]] {{math|''r'' {{=}} {{sfrac|''a''|{{lower|0.2em|{{sqrt|''θ''}}}}}}}} can be converted to [[Cartesian coordinate system|Cartesian coordinates]] like any other spiral with the relationships {{math|''x'' {{=}} ''r'' cos ''θ''}} and {{math|''y'' {{=}} ''r'' sin ''θ''}}. With this conversion we get the parametric representations of the curve:

: <math>\begin{align}
 x &= \frac{a}{\sqrt{\theta}} \cos\theta, \\
 y &= \frac{a}{\sqrt{\theta}} \sin\theta. \\
\end{align}</math>

These equations can in turn be rearranged to an equation in {{mvar|x}} and {{mvar|y}}:

: <math>\frac{y}{x} = \tan\left( \frac{a^2}{x^2 + y^2} \right).</math>

{{hidden begin|title=Derivation of the equation in Cartesian coordinates|showhide=left}}
# Divide <math>y</math> by <math>x</math>:<math>\frac{y}{x} = \frac{\frac{a}{\sqrt{\theta}} \sin\theta}{\frac{a}{\sqrt{\theta}} \cos\theta} \Rightarrow \frac{y}{x} = \tan\theta.</math>
# Solve the equation of the lituus spiral in polar coordinates: <math>r = \frac{a}{\sqrt{\theta}} \Leftrightarrow \theta = \frac{a^2}{r^2}.</math>
# Substitute <math>\theta = \frac{a^2}{r^2}</math>: <math>\frac{y}{x} = \tan\left( \frac{a^2}{r^2} \right).</math>
# Substitute <math>r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}</math>: <math>\frac{y}{x} = \tan\left( \frac{a^2}{\left( \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \right)^2} \right) \Rightarrow \frac{y}{x} = \tan\left( \frac{a^2}{x^2 + y^2} \right).</math>
{{hidden end}}

== Geometrical properties ==

=== Curvature ===
The [[curvature]] of the lituus spiral can be determined using the formula<ref name=":0">{{Mathworld |id=Lituus |access-date=2023-02-04}}</ref>

: <math>\kappa = \left( 8 \theta^2 - 2 \right) \left( \frac{\theta}{1 + 4 \theta^2} \right)^\frac32.</math>

=== Arc length ===
In general, the [[arc length]] of the lituus spiral cannot be expressed as a [[closed-form expression]], but the [[arc length]] of the lituus spiral can be represented as a formula using the [[Hypergeometric function|Gaussian hypergeometric function]]:

: <math>L = 2 \sqrt{\theta} \cdot \operatorname{_2 F_1}\left( -\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{1}{4}; \frac{3}{4}; -\frac{1}{4 \theta^2} \right) - 2 \sqrt{\theta_0} \cdot \operatorname{_2 F_1}\left( -\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{1}{4}; \frac{3}{4}; -\frac{1}{4 \theta_0^2} \right),</math>

where the arc length is measured from {{math|''θ'' {{=}} ''θ''<sub>0</sub>}}.<ref name=":0" />

=== Tangential angle ===
The tangential angle (see [[Pitch angle of a spiral]]) of the lituus spiral can be determined using the formula<ref name=":0" />

: <math>\phi = \theta - \arctan 2\theta.</math>
